long_biography.plain_text:
Numbers came before building sites. Mitterrand studied mathematics, statistics and management in France and the United States, then spent brief periods in leasing and property finance. In the early 1970s he created a housing business that later added offices, entered Spain and Germany, and tested itself in public markets.

Four decades at the helm ended with an orderly generational handover. Mitterrand shifted into oversight while Moïse assumed executive control; the enterprise later changed its name and remained concentrated in family holding companies. Away from commercial work, he directed an École Polytechnique fundraising campaign and created a foundation supporting construction, health, education and employment projects in disadvantaged communities.
